explanation: A metal rod on the roof, wired to the ground, gives lightning an easy path to earth around the building. Franklin chose not to patent it.

claims.text: Benjamin Franklin invented the lightning rod, in the early 1750s, to protect buildings from lightning.
Franklin did not invent the fuse box, the weather vane or the surge protector.
A lightning rod is a metal rod joined by a conductor to the ground, giving lightning a path to earth that bypasses the building.
Franklin did not patent the lightning rod.
